title: 6.10.10 Lab: Pick a mode
description: A title screen that waits for a key: 1 plays with the mouse, 2 with the arrow keys. Write the choices, read the key, and send R back to the title. With a note on prompt().

steps.title: The title words
steps.instructions:
The starter is your finished game from 6.10.9 with one more state, `'title'`. `state` starts as `'title'`, and while it is, `draw()` calls `pickMode()` and moves nothing. `pickMode()` is empty, so right now the game waits on the title forever. This is the title screen of 6.6.11, and the way out of it is a key, as in 6.6.16.

In `drawTop()`, when `state` is `'title'`, write the name of the game and the two choices: `Press 1 to play with the mouse` and `Press 2 to play with the arrow keys`. Put them under the wall, between y 200 and 280, so they do not cover the bricks (the ball waits at y 300). Run it: the words show, and nothing moves yet.
hints: `if (state === 'title') { ... }` with two or three `text(...)` lines inside, as in 6.6.11.
`textSize(28)` before the name makes it bigger; set it back to 16 for the two lines.

steps.title: A key picks the mode
steps.instructions:
In `pickMode()`: when `kb.presses('1')` is true, set `control` to `'mouse'` and `state` to `'play'`; when `kb.presses('2')` is true, set `control` to `'keys'` and `state` to `'play'`. A number key's name is its digit in quotes, `'1'`, the same way `'r'` names the R key. Use `kb.presses`, not `kb.pressing`: one press is one choice (6.3.3). Run it and press 1: the game starts with the mouse. Run again and press 2: the arrow keys steer the paddle.

**A note on prompt().** You could ask with `prompt('Press 1 for the mouse or 2 for the keys')` instead; the sketch allows it. It gives back what was typed as text, a string, which is why 3.1.9 wrapped it in `Number(prompt(...))`. So you compare with `'1'`, not `1`. But a prompt freezes the whole game until it is answered, it looks like the browser and not like your game, and a mistyped answer leaves you with nothing to start. A title screen keeps the game running and shows the choice in your game's own style, which is why games use one. The check accepts either; if you try a prompt, put it in `pickMode()` in place of the two key tests.
hints: The second `if` is the same with `'2'` and `'keys'`.

steps.title: R goes back to the title
steps.instructions: When a game ends, the starter's R starts the next one straight away (`startGame();` then `state = 'play';` in `draw()`). Change it so R sets up the new game and goes back to the title, so the next player can choose: `state = 'title'` instead of `'play'`. Play to the end (miss three times to be quick), press R, and the title comes back with a whole wall and three lives.
hints: `startGame()` still builds the new wall and resets the score and the lives; the title then waits for 1 or 2.
